evidence.excerpt: They report member churn to the board every quarter, it had ticked up two quarters running
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Trigger: board-reported churn rose two quarters in a row.

evidence.excerpt: somebody finally split it into people who cancelled and people whose card just failed.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Churn was split into cancellations versus failed cards; this exposed the payment-failure problem.

evidence.excerpt: members who never meant to leave.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Maya, head of digital
evidence.note: Maya's own phrase for failed-card churn; the rep called it a great line.

evidence.excerpt: I want to say a third of the churn? Don't quote me. It was in her board deck.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Hedged recollection of the size of the failed-card bucket; rep says the board deck has it.

evidence.excerpt: Two hundred and ten K ACV.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Deal size stated as ACV.

evidence.excerpt: that's memberships only, the front desks aren't in it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Only part of the business is in the deal value.

evidence.excerpt: She ran the evaluation, she was in every meeting, she's the one who told me where we stood.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Basis for naming Maya as decider: she ran the evaluation and updated the rep.

evidence.excerpt: She said it was her call.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Maya, head of digital
evidence.note: Maya reportedly claimed the decision; relayed secondhand, not verbatim.

evidence.excerpt: Global Payments was already in there, through the studio software.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Incumbent already embedded via the studio management software.

evidence.excerpt: they came back with a rate review and a new terminal bundle for the front desks, on a longer contract.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Maya, head of digital
evidence.note: Incumbent's counteroffer as Maya told the rep; rep did not see it.

evidence.excerpt: I didn't see any of it. That's her telling me.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep flags the competitor information as secondhand.

evidence.excerpt: My read is they were rattled, but that's my read, not hers.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep's own interpretation of the incumbent's state; separated from Maya's view.

evidence.excerpt: Before that meeting it was all failed payments and retries.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Customer questions before meeting the competitor focused on failed payments.

evidence.excerpt: After it was, what readers do you have, do they work inside our studio software, what's the contract term, what does it cost to get out.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Questions shifted to hardware, integration and exit costs after the competitor meeting.

evidence.excerpt: Greg asked about termination fees twice.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Greg's concern was cost of leaving the incumbent.

evidence.excerpt: The controller.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Greg's role is controller.

evidence.excerpt: Tobi, took an export of one month of their failed renewals and showed which ones were the kind that usually come back with a retry or an updated card.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: The data session on the customer's own failed renewals drew the reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Their file, not our average.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: The demo used customer data, not generic averages.

evidence.excerpt: Greg hadn't said a word in two meetings, and he asked for the spreadsheet.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Greg, previously silent, engaged on the data.

evidence.excerpt: I opened with the global slide. They have studios in the US and a handful in Canada.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Global slide got silence; the customer is nearly all North American.

evidence.excerpt: And when I said 'unified commerce,'
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep used the phrase 'unified commerce' in the pitch.

evidence.excerpt: is that the readers?
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Maya, head of digital
evidence.note: Maya translated 'unified commerce' into hardware terms.

evidence.excerpt: Before that I honestly thought we were there to keep the incumbent honest.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep believed we were a pricing lever against the incumbent until the data session.

evidence.excerpt: The paper had gone to Greg and it sat with him for two weeks.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Contract sat with Greg for two weeks without movement.

evidence.excerpt: Then we did the data session, and four days later it was signed.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Signature followed the data session by four days.

evidence.excerpt: His signature's on it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Greg signed the contract.

evidence.excerpt: Maya chose us. Greg decided whether anybody got chosen.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep's revised view after prompting: split authority between Maya and Greg.

evidence.excerpt: We couldn't show that live. It runs through a partner integration, and the partner did a call the week after.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Could not demo the reader inside their studio software; partner call came later.

evidence.excerpt: It nearly cost us.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep's judgement that the demo gap almost lost the deal.

evidence.excerpt: the studio managers will revolt.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Maya, head of digital
evidence.note: Maya's objection to front-desk staff using two screens.

evidence.excerpt: They saw the partner's demo. Not in their own setup.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Customer never saw the reader in their own environment before signing.

evidence.excerpt: what they signed is memberships. Online billing went first. The studios are phase two.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Partial win: online membership billing only; studios deferred.

evidence.excerpt: Still Global.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Incumbent still processes at the front desks.

evidence.excerpt: Not yet. It depends on the partner piece.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: No date for phase two; contingent on the partner integration.

evidence.excerpt: Can we do that one over Slack? I've got a customer call at the top of the hour and I need five minutes to prep.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: the rep
evidence.note: Rep deferred the customer-wording question; the interview ended without an answer.

contradictions.what: Rep first named Maya as the final decider, then admitted Greg held the contract for two weeks and signed it, so Greg decided whether anyone got chosen.
Rep thought we were only keeping the incumbent honest, yet the deal signed four days after the data session; the rep's read of the evaluation changed.
Deal is described as won, but only memberships (210K ACV) are signed; front desks remain with Global and phase two has no date.

dodges.question: How big was that bucket?
dodges.what: Gave a hedged 'a third of the churn?' with 'don't quote me', pointing to Maya's board deck instead of a firm number.

dodges.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
dodges.what: Answered 'Maya' based on her own claim, then contradicted this at T22 after the Greg signature came out.

dodges.question: Last one. What exact words did they—
dodges.what: Deflected the customer-language question to Slack because of a call; it was never answered.

language_pairs.theirs: members who never meant to leave
the studio managers will revolt (two screens at the front desk)

outcome_signals.what: Won: contract signed by Greg four days after the data session.
Partial: only memberships and online billing signed (210K ACV); front desks are not included.
Front desks are phase two with no date, still on Global, dependent on the partner integration the customer has only seen as a partner demo.
